issues.detail: Description/notes attribute 'accept/decline determinations under NAIC Model #275' to the F&G Built In posting; the fetched posting references the NAIC Annuity Transactions Model Regulation without naming '#275'. The second source (NAIC page) does name Model #275, so the claim is jointly supported — attribution imprecision only, not an ungrounded claim.

The classificationFlag rationale says the Ascot posting places 'bordereaux data-quality validation at the core of the role'; the fetched posting mentions 'oversight of bordereaux data quality and timely submission' but leans administrative-support. Flag direction (Participant -> Owner) is still reasonable and packet-grounded (task 'Validate Bordereaux Data Quality And Completeness' is Participant in the packet); rationale is mildly overstated. Note: the posting was removed 2026-06-03 but the URL still resolves with full JD content.

Description states duties 'align with the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law's requirement for a designated leader of the insurer's information security program with board-level reporting'. The cited NAIC page confirms Model Law #668 and its information-security-program requirement but does not itself show the designated-leader/board-reporting detail (that lives in the Model Law text). Claim is true of the Model Law but over-attributed to the fetched page.

roleLevel 'Senior Leadership' is valid per the verification enum (Executive | Senior Leadership | Manager | Individual Contributor) but is absent from org-catalog.json roleLevelVocab, which instead lists 'Management'. Vocabulary drift between the catalog and the research output schema is worth reconciling before load.

Notes claim 'Sources validate the schedule/rate-table, statement, reconciliation, and chargeback scope'. Fetched coverage is thinner: Core Commissions covers chargebacks and carrier statements only briefly and does not substantively address reconciliation or rate tables; InsurTech Express covers schedules/reconciliation/statements but not chargebacks. Every element has some support across the two sources combined, but the validation claim is generous. Description itself remains packet-grounded.
